nt: Alternate translation: [So he exclaimed about Ham]
Alternate translation: [I hereby ask God to curse] or [May God curse]

In [verses 25–27](../09/25.md), Canaan probably represents Ham and all of Ham’s descendants (the Canaanites), who will serve Shem and Japheth and all their descendants. You could put that information in a footnote.
Alternate translation: [I proclaim that he will be]

The Hebrew word here can mean either **slave** or “servant.” Slaves in the Old Testament were usually treated well and were not much different than servants, sometimes even becoming like members of their owner’s family. But they were of lower status than their masters, which is part of how Ham’s family is being cursed. Alternate translation: [the lowest slave]
[Verses 26](../09/26.md) and [27](../09/27.md) show that **his brothers** probably refers here to Shem and Japheth (who were Canaan’s uncles) and their descendants.

Although many English translations have “Blessed be” here instead of **Praised be**, the word used in the Hebrew text means “praise” when people are acting towards God (as here), and it means “bless” when God is acting towards people (as in Genesis [1:28](../01/28.md); [5:2](../05/02.md); [9:1](../09/01.md)).
